evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/syndication.rs:289 — `SyndicationService::process_syndication_job` is the only code that would actually push a listing to an external portal and flip syndication status, but it has ZERO production callers (grep for `process_syndication_job` across backend yields only its own definition). The enqueue side IS production-reachable: routes/listings.rs:546 calls `create_status_change_jobs` and routes/listings.rs:661 calls `create_publish_jobs` when a manager publishes a listing to SReality/Bezrealitky/Nehnutelnosti/Reality-Portal. Those insert rows into the `syndication` background-job queue (SYNDICATION_QUEUE, syndication.rs:15), but no scheduler task or background worker drains that queue (grep for `syndication` under services/scheduler/ is empty; the BackgroundScheduler has no syndication job). Net effect: listings are never actually syndicated and the background_jobs table accumulates unclaimed syndication rows indefinitely, silently — the manager sees the publish succeed with no error.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/syndication.rs:287-333 — even if a worker were wired up, `process_syndication_job` is an explicit placeholder: the PUBLISH branch logs `"Simulate publishing to portal"`, fabricates a fake external id (`format!("{}_{}", payload.portal, uuid::Uuid::new_v4())`, line 318), and calls `update_syndication_status(..., SYNCED, Some(&external_id), ...)`. STATUS_CHANGE/UPDATE/REMOVE branches (lines 334-403) likewise flip the row to SYNCED/REMOVED with no real portal API call. So wiring it as-is would record fabricated SYNCED state (and bogus external ids) for portals the listing was never actually sent to. Fix: implement the real portal API calls (or keep the queue unprocessed but surface a 'syndication not yet available' state to the manager instead of silently enqueuing dead jobs).

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/actions/email.rs:86-112 — the workflow-automation `SEND_EMAIL` action executor (`EmailExecutor::execute`) never sends an email. It substitutes the template, validates the `to` address, then just `tracing::info!("Workflow sending email")` and returns `ActionResult::success(json!({"sent_to": to, "subject": subject, "sent_at": chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339(), ...}))`. The comment at line 96 states 'Simulate email sending (in production, integrate with EmailService)'. This executor IS registered in the production default registry (services/actions/mod.rs:204 `registry.register(Box::new(EmailExecutor::new()))`), so any automation rule a manager builds with a send-email action reports success and records a fabricated `sent_at` while no email is ever dispatched. An actual `EmailService` exists and is used elsewhere (services/email.rs) but is not injected here. Fix: inject EmailService into EmailExecutor and send, or make the action return a not-implemented ActionError instead of fabricated success so rule authors aren't misled.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/actions/notification.rs:161-198 — the workflow-automation `NOTIFICATION` action executor (`NotificationExecutor::execute`) is the same shipped-stub pattern as the email action: role targets (line 117-118 'Would send to users with role') and building-resident targets (line 128-129 'Would send to building residents') are only `tracing::debug!`-logged, never resolved; the execute body logs `"Workflow sending notification"` (line 183) and returns `ActionResult::success(...)` (line 198) with the comment 'In production, this would actually send notifications via the notification service'. This executor is also registered in the production default registry (services/actions/mod.rs:205 `registry.register(Box::new(NotificationExecutor::new()))`). A real `NotificationService` / push_fanout pipeline exists in the codebase but is not wired in here. Net effect: automation rules with a notification action report success but deliver nothing to tenants/managers. Fix: inject the notification service and dispatch, or return a not-implemented ActionError rather than fabricated success.
